chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khurasani, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the Qa'im, when he rises in Makkah and intends to proceed to al-Kufah, his caller will call out: Lo, let none of you carry any food or drink. And he will carry the stone of Musa ibn 'Imran, and it is the load of a camel. He will not alight at any stopping-place except that a spring will gush forth from it. So whoever is hungry will be satisfied, and whoever is thirsty will be quenched. Thus it will be their provision until they come down at al-Najaf, behind al-Kufah.

key_terms.النَّجَفَ: al-Najaf, the place where they finally encamp
key_terms.الْقَائِمَ: the Qa'im, the one who will arise from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: al-Kufah, the destination toward which he proceeds
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, the place of his rising mentioned here
key_terms.حَجَرَ مُوسَى بْنِ عِمْرَانَ: the stone of Musa ibn 'Imran عليه السلام, serving here as a miraculous means of provision
key_terms.عَيْنٌ: a spring of water bursting forth
key_terms.وِقْرُ بَعِيرٍ: the load of a camel, indicating its great weight

ai.seo_question: How will the Qa'im عليه السلام and his followers be provided for on the journey from Makkah to al-Kufah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a sign associated with the Qa'im عليه السلام during his movement from Makkah to al-Kufah. It presents a miraculous provision through the stone of Musa ibn 'Imran عليه السلام, from which a spring emerges to feed and quench his followers, highlighting divine support and continuity with the signs of earlier Prophets عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abu Saeed Al Khurasany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The Qaim<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> arises at Makkah and intends to divert towards Al-Kufa, a Caller would Call out: ‘Indeed! Not one of you should carry the food nor any drink, and he should carry a rock of Musa<sup>as</sup> Bin Imran<sup>as</sup>, and it would be the load of a camel!’ So they would not descend at an encampment except a spring would burst out from it. So whoever would be hungry, would be satiated, and the one who was thirsty would be quenched. Thus, it would be their provision until they encamp at Al-Najaf, which is behind Al-Kufa’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa‘dan from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Qasim from abu Sa‘id al-Khurasani from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said that abu Ja‘far (a.s.) has said the following.

“When al-Qa’im (the one who will rise to establish the kingdom of Allah on earth) will rise in Makka and about to leave for Kufa a caller will up on him, “No one of you carry any food and water with you. No one carry the rock of Moses ibn ‘Imran. It a full load for a camel. Wherever you will disembark there will be a water fountain. Whoever will be hungry it will satisfy him and whoever will be thirsty it quench his thirst. It will be their supplies until they will arrive in Najaf behind al-Kufa.”
